# Supporting services — domain, scope, arm, sequence

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/build-supporting-reference.py — do not edit. -->

**171 services, 974 collectable types.** A supporting
service governs the estate rather than serving traffic in it: it holds
`kind: rule` in the model, and that is what puts it on a border rail rather
than inline among the workloads.

Four things decide where one draws, and each comes from somewhere different:

| Column | Answers | Comes from |
|---|---|---|
| **Scope** | *which box* — whose border it hangs on | `roles.*.container` |
| **Arm** | *which side* of that box | `rail_slots` — from the DOMAIN |
| **Slot** | *where on that side* | `rail_slots.slots` |
| **Domain** | *what it is* — the heading on the tab | `taxonomy` in the binding |
| **Seq** | *where in the stack* along that arm | order of the `taxonomy` block |

**Seq is relative, not absolute.** It is a reading order, not a slot: if the
estate has no `firewall`, `routing` moves up and takes its place. Nothing is
reserved and no gap is drawn for something that is not there — an empty tab
would be a claim about an estate nobody has.

The numbers come from the *order of the taxonomy block in the model*, which is
the same list the engine sorts by. Moving a line in that block moves a tab on
the canvas; there is no second table to keep in step.

## What each arm means

| Arm | Question it answers | On the canvas |
|---|---|---|
| **E · east** | who may act, and what is sealed | 181 types |
| **W · west** | how it is built, run and owned | 669 types |
| **S · south** | how traffic leaves, and would we notice | 124 types |
| **N · north** | doors only — no rule tabs | 0 types |

## How to read a rail

Each row above is one **tab** on the border named in *Scope*, on the side named
in *Arm*, stacked in *Seq* order. The tab is open on the side facing the box, so
it reads as attached to that container rather than floating near it, and it is
tinted by the code family its domain belongs to. Clicking one lists the
resources.

A resource governed by one of these carries its **code** — `sg-2`, `iam-1`,
`kms-1` — in the same hue as the arm the governing resource rides, so a reader
goes to the right border without reading a word. Codes are only issued to
governing resources with at least one **drawn** member: a code pointing at
something nobody can find is worse than no code.
